transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having some thoughts that have started to worry me. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but sometimes I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up.

And… on the drive home, I’ll wonder if my family, or even my students, would be better off without me. I don’t want to act on it, I really don’t. It just scares me that the thoughts are there at all. Is that… okay to say?
Have you had any thoughts of killing yourself?

I… I don’t think I want to kill myself. I really don’t want to act on anything. But I have been having thoughts like… it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or sometimes driving home I wonder if my family or my students would be better off without me.

I’m sorry, I know that sounds awful. It scares me that I even think it.
Have you had any moments of wanting to end your life?

I… yes, sort of. Not like I have a plan or anything I’m about to do, but I have had moments where I think it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes when I’m driving home, I wonder if my family or my students would be better off without me.

I’m sorry… I know that’s a lot to say. It scares me, because I don’t want to act on it.
Have you been feeling depressed most days?

I’m… not sure how to answer that properly. I mean, I’ve been low a lot, I guess, but I don’t know if it’s “depressed” most days exactly. I don’t want to overstate it.

It’s just been harder to feel like myself lately. Does that make sense?
Before this recent period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt like this for a couple of weeks or longer?

I’m not sure… not exactly like this, I don’t think. I’ve had stressful patches before, like anyone, but I don’t know if they lasted a couple of weeks in this same way.

Sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?
Did something stressful happen in your life shortly before these thoughts and low feelings started?

I think so, yes. It wasn’t one big dramatic thing, but… about a year and seven months ago I took over the STEM assessment redesign at school, on top of my normal teaching load.

I kept telling myself it was manageable and that I should be able to handle it, but that’s around when things started to feel heavier. Is that the kind of stressful event you mean?
Do your low feelings seem mainly related to the extra responsibilities at school?

Mostly, yes, I think it does connect to that. It’s been going on since I took on the STEM assessment redesign alongside my normal teaching work… so, about a year and seven months now.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming work entirely, but that’s when it seemed to start getting heavier. Does that answer it?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I think I have, though I feel a bit bad saying that because I still try to show up for things.

I used to really look forward to softball, book club, working in my garden, and helping with robotics club. Now I mostly either go through the motions, or I cancel because it just doesn’t feel enjoyable the way it used to. Is that what you mean?
When you’re away from work, do you still feel low?

I’m… not completely sure how to separate it, honestly. Being away from work can help a little sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it just disappears.

I still can feel low at home or on weekends, but I keep thinking maybe that’s just me not switching off properly. I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you’re looking for.
If the school workload were taken away, do you think you would still feel this low?

I’m not sure, honestly. I’d like to think I’d feel a lot better if the workload was taken away… and maybe I would.

But I don’t know if it would completely lift. I suppose I’m a bit worried that saying that sounds dramatic, because work really has been the main thing. I just can’t confidently say, “Yes, I’d be fine,” if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling tired or low on energy a lot lately?

Yes… I mean, I’m still getting through the day, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But lately by the time I’ve taught my classes and sat through a department meeting, my body just feels really heavy.

Then even normal things, like making dinner or answering a few parent emails, feel like I’m climbing a hill. I don’t know if that counts as low energy, but it’s definitely more than just being a bit tired.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

A bit, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, because I do get into bed and I’m exhausted, but then my brain just doesn’t seem to stop.

I’ll lie there replaying assessment deadlines or something I said in class that didn’t go well, and it can take ages to fall asleep. And then sometimes I wake up around 4 in the morning and… I’m sort of just awake after that, not really properly getting back to sleep. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes… a bit. I mean, I can still do my work, mostly, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely unable to function.

But I’ve noticed when I’m marking, I’ll read the same student response three or four times and still feel like I don’t actually know what score to give it. And then even small decisions can take me ages — like choosing which lab supplies to order, I can sort of get stuck on that for an hour.

I don’t know if that’s concentration exactly, but it does feel like my thinking is slower than it usually is.
Have these low feelings and loss of interest been present nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s not like every single minute of every day, but it’s been there most days, definitely more than two weeks.

Honestly, it’s been going on for quite a while — probably about a year and seven months now, since I took over the STEM assessment redesign on top of my normal teaching load. I kept thinking it was just a busy term or that I should be handling it better, but it hasn’t really lifted.
Before this current stretch, was there ever another time in your life when you felt this same kind of low mood and loss of interest for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I don’t think there was another time that was quite like this, not for that long.

I mean, I’ve had stressful patches before where I felt low or a bit flat, but I can’t really remember it being this same sort of sustained loss of interest for two weeks or more. Does that answer it properly?
Have you been feeling worthless or like you’re a burden to other people?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound dramatic.

It’s more like, if a lesson doesn’t go well or a student looks confused, I take it really personally. I’ll think, “That’s proof I’m letting everyone down,” and then I keep replaying it afterwards, like I’m a terrible teacher… and a terrible mother too, somehow.

I know that probably sounds over the top, and I can usually tell myself other people wouldn’t see it that way, but in the moment it feels quite true. Does that make sense?
Have you ever tried to end your life in the past?

No… I mean, I haven’t tried to end my life before.

I’m sorry, that’s hard to say properly. I’m here because I’ve started catching myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, and sometimes on the drive home I wonder whether my family or my students would be better off without me. That really scares me, because I don’t want to act on it. Does that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
For at least two weeks during this time, have you felt sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

I… I’m not completely sure how to answer that.

I have felt down, yes, but I don’t know if I’d confidently say it’s been most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. Some days I can sort of keep going and seem normal enough, so I wonder if I’m overstating it.

Could you maybe explain what counts as “most of the day”?
On those days when you feel down, does that low mood last for most of the day?

I think… on the days it’s there, it does tend to hang around for a lot of the day, yes.

Not every single minute, and I can still teach or answer emails and sort of look normal, but underneath it’s there. I’m not sure if that counts as “most of the day,” though — I don’t want to exaggerate.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt sad, down, or empty nearly every day?

Nearly every day… I’m not sure. I don’t want to say yes if that’s not quite accurate.

It’s been there a lot, more than I’d like to admit, but I’m having trouble judging whether it’s nearly every day or just most days. I suppose I may be minimizing it a bit, but… I don’t know. Is it okay if I’m not completely sure?
